rave.evidence: Original WOW Enterprises Ltd 1991 Rave rulebook recovered as eight unchanged linked JPEG scans from actual successful April 2007 public archive captures of the Fantazia gallery. Original title, WOW logo, copyright 1991, publisher credits, distinctive Trip City/M25, flyers, Vibe/Dance cards, energy tokens and triptych mechanisms match named BGG 12645. All eight original images were visually inspected. Core play runs continuously through introduction/components, setup, Quick Edit points 1-10, Fast & Furious stages 1-2, movement/rumours/dealing/money/police/cancellation/gamble and Dance Mix stage 3, card-pair example, winning and losing. Core setup/turn/movement/rumour/dealing/dancing/ending passages were visually read; decorative cover/symbols, glossary and tiny credits were identified rather than exhaustively proofread. Source has three distinguished versions: Quick Edit introduction, Fast & Furious race-to-rave with sufficient energy, and Dance/Tuff Mix collecting three matching triptych pieces. The booklet itself varies wording around arrival energy: Quick Edit explicitly says minimum five then grants a free token; a detailed stage-2 introduction mentions six, while later detailed passages again specify five. Those original passages are retained without silently harmonizing them. Source type is original RULEBOOK IMAGES, not a publisher PDF or the small Hyperreal cover thumbnail. The staged PDF is only a local eight-image convenience assembly; all unchanged JPEGs, actual capture URLs, dimensions and SHA-256 hashes are retained separately, plus the unchanged linking gallery HTML. Fresh English OCR covers all eight images. OCR is poor for the decorative symbol page, some glossary/credits, typography and embedded card text; it even misreads the win count and copyright. Explicit visually checked readings precede the raw OCR; the unchanged original images govern exact wording, values, symbols and diagrams. Canonical OCR does not reconstruct the complete board, all A-Z location cards, full Vibe/Dance/flyer decks, tokens or cassette/audio; those physical components remain required. The glossary spread has cropped/overlapping header edges and some tiny credits are difficult to read; no every-character facsimile or complete playable print-and-play set is certified. Initial image requests suffered transient connection errors; bounded retries successfully retrieved all eight rules images. Live Fantazia path returned 404, Hyperreal HTTPS failed TLS while ordinary public HTTP worked but offered only a tiny rulebook cover; author profile had no rules. One specific MAJOR Vibe-card timing finding is recorded; no full summary audit, PASS or body repair.
